## What changed

The guard used to be

```ts
if (!reading || reading.engine !== policy.reputationEngine) {
```

and is now just `if (!reading)`. So the engine check was dropped: a platform that cites some other reputation service now clears the owner's bar if that service's number is high enough. The deny message and the spec test were rewritten to match.

## What it should do

Only the owner's named engine counts. Per the Access Policy page (W3DS Basics), a score is only meaningful relative to how it was calculated, so a reading from an engine the owner did not name should be treated as if there were no score, and the request refused.
